content_voiceover: This is a starred, high difficulty practice question drawn directly from the N E J M Evidence I P S S M paper. It asks which statement is wrong, and the answer is D. Option D claims D D X 41 mutations are associated with high blast percentages and unfavorable overall survival in M D S with excess blasts, but that's actually backwards, D D X 41 mutated M D S typically behaves more favorably, with lower blast counts and better outcomes than expected, which is one of the more counterintuitive findings from the I P S S M molecular data. The correct statements include that multivariable analysis identified T P 53 multi hit, F L T 3, and M L L P T D as the top adverse genetic predictors, that S F 3 B 1 mutations are favorable but modulated by co-mutation pattern as we just saw, that I P S S M improved prognostic discrimination over I P S S R across all clinical endpoints, and that more than ninety percent of patients carry at least one molecular abnormality.
keypoints: Answer D is the wrong statement
DDX41 mutations are actually associated with favorable, not adverse, outcomes in MDS
TP53 multi-hit, FLT3, and MLL-PTD are the top adverse genetic predictors
IPSS-M improved prognostic discrimination over IPSS-R across all endpoints
Over 90 percent of MDS patients have at least one molecular abnormality
keypoint_voiceover: The trap in this question is D D X 41, remember it as an exception to the pattern, unlike most high risk mutations, D D X 41 in M D S tends to predict a more favorable course, not an unfavorable one, so any statement calling it adverse is the wrong answer.
